units.text: INT. DEEP-SEA CORE LAB - NIGHT
A pressurized steel cylinder, lit a sickly amber.
Pipes sweat.
Through a single thick porthole, the black water presses close, and something pale drifts past and is gone.
DR. SABINE ARGYLE (40s, cropped hair, a sleeve of burn scars) kneels at a sample drawer.
At the console, her partner TEODOR MARSH (50s, round glasses) taps a failing readout.
Between them hovers the lab's AI, VESPER, a small amber light in a ceiling lattice.
The floor shivers.
A bolt pings off the wall.
That wasn't the pump.
units.name: SABINE

units.text: That wasn't the pump.
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: Hull stress at nine percent above tolerance.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: The two scientists exchange a look.
Sabine slams the drawer shut; Teodor lunges for the console.
They collide in the narrow aisle, tangling arms, and both catch the same railing as the lab pitches.
Vesper, which section?
units.name: SABINE

units.text: Vesper, which section?
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: Aft. The sample bay.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: The porthole darkens.
A pale shape presses against it, slow, deliberate.
The shiver in the floor becomes a groan.
Seal it.
units.name: SABINE

units.text: Seal it now!
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: They throw their shoulders against the bulkhead wheel together, and it turns, screeching, and the amber light flickers and holds.
